# Data Visualization

## Assignment 2: Good and Bad Data Visualization

### Requirements:

- Data visualizations are important tools for communication and convincing; we need to be able to evaluate the ways that data are presented in visual form to be critical consumers of information 
- To test your evaluation skills, locate two public data visualizations online, one good and one bad  
    - You can find data visualizations at https://public.tableau.com/app/discover or https://datavizproject.com/, or anywhere else you like! 
- For each visualization (good and bad):  
    - Explain (with reference to material covered up to date, along with readings and other scholarly sources, as needed) why you classified that visualization the way you did.
      ```
Example 1: Bad visualization: https://public.tableau.com/app/profile/vlastimil/viz/MILK/Dashboard2

The author indents to portay the cyclic effects of weather as well as the trend across time (10 years) on the nutritional value of milk. With this goal in mind, the data is plotted on a circular axis. 

Example 2: Good visualization: https://100.datavizproject.com/data-type/viz44/

I like the above visualization as I think it as a neat way to emphasize the rate of change in percentage. The 3D plot neatly picturizes both the peaks at two different time points as well as the percentage of change. It nicely illustrates how one can liverage the third dimension to bring out new information compared to a classic 2D plot.

      ```
    - How could this data visualization have been improved?  
      ```
    
Example 1: bad visualizartion. I would like to argue that this is a bad idea. The trends can be better captured by portraying the data in a standard rectangular XY plot. Even for cyclic seasonal variations, it is easy to visualize that on a rectangular plot. Having it plotted circually, in my opinion, makes it harder to observe the changes w.r.t some reference point. 
  
Example 2: good visualization: It feel like the authors wanted particularly bring out the percentage of change aspect and not the absolute value, eventhough the absolute value is also a vital information that is important in a lot of situations. I think the perspective of the graph needs some adjustment to make it more easy to follow. The sides of the 3D walls are not colored, I wonder if they could be color to emphasize the absolute value.   

      ```
- Word count should not exceed (as a maximum) 500 words for each visualization (i.e. 
300 words for your good example and 500 for your bad example)
